{
  "research_question": "Does the stimulation paradigm (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) have a statistically significant effect on mouse navigation performance metrics: Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Perform a one-way ANOVA for each of the five response variables with 'Stim Paradigm' as the independent factor.",
    "For 'Success' (binary 0/1) and 'Path Efficiency' (highly skewed, min 0.000928, max 29.817273), note that the distributional assumptions of ANOVA (normality, homoscedasticity) are likely violated; consider non-parametric alternatives (Kruskal-Wallis) or Generalized Linear Models (GLM) with appropriate link functions as primary analysis if diagnostics fail.",
    "For 'Time-to-Target' (right-skewed distribution given max=201.39 vs mean=2.80), apply a log-transformation (e.g., log(Time-to-Target + 1)) before running ANOVA to stabilize variance and approach normality.",
    "For 'Average Speed' and 'AD', verify normality and equal variance; if assumptions hold, proceed with standard F-test ANOVA."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check for normality of residuals for each transformed response variable using Q-Q plots or Shapiro-Wilk tests (critical for 'Success' and 'Path Efficiency' without transformation).",
    "Check for homogeneity of variances (homoscedasticity) using Levene's test or Bartlett's test across the five paradigm groups.",
    "Verify independence of observations (assumed based on data structure, though check for repeated measures within 'Mouse' if multiple trials per mouse exist).",
    "Inspect residual plots for linearity and outliers, particularly in the 'Time-to-Target' and 'Path Efficiency' groups where ranges are wide."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If the omnibus F-test for any variable is significant (p < 0.05), conduct pairwise comparisons using Tukey's HSD (Honestly Significant Difference) test to control family-wise error rate.",
    "For 'Success', if treating as binomial, use post-hoc contrasts via GLM (e.g., Bonferroni-corrected pairwise comparisons of logits).",
    "Report effect sizes (e.g., eta-squared or Cohen's d) for significant group differences, noting the large sample size of 'Combined' (n=48846) versus others.",
    "Specifically compare 'Sham' against all other conditions given the stark mean difference in 'Success' (0.27 vs ~0.67-0.78) observed in the summary statistics."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Expect a significant main effect for 'Success' and 'Time-to-Target', given the substantial differences in means between 'Sham' (Success=0.27, Time=4.68) and 'Combined' (Success=0.78, Time=2.56).",
    "Expect 'Sham' to perform significantly worse than 'Combined', 'ICMS Only', 'Dim Visual Only', and 'Bright Visual Only' on 'Success' and 'Time-to-Target'.",
    "Expect 'Average Speed' and 'Path Efficiency' to show lower means for 'Sham' compared to active stimulation groups, though the effect magnitude may be smaller than for 'Success'.",
    "Expect 'AD' (angular dispersion) to be higher (worse) in 'Sham' (0.236) compared to 'Combined' (0.399) and others, though the direction depends on whether higher AD indicates less precision or more exploration; assuming higher AD = less precise, 'Sham' shows lower AD which might indicate restricted movement or different behavioral strategy, requiring interpretation of the raw score definition.",
    "The 'Dim Visual Only' and 'Bright Visual Only' groups show similar performance profiles compared to 'ICMS Only', suggesting distinct differences from 'Combined' and 'Sham'."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "The 'Success' variable is binary, violating the normality assumption of ANOVA; results for this variable are potentially invalid without using non-parametric or GLM methods.",
    "The 'Path Efficiency' variable has extreme outliers (max=29.8) and a wide range, likely violating homoscedasticity and normality assumptions without transformation.",
    "Potential confounding by 'Mouse' ID: The dataset contains multiple levels of mice (8 levels), and if multiple trials are nested within mice, a standard one-way ANOVA ignores the within-subject correlation, inflating Type I error. A mixed-effects model with 'Mouse' as a random effect is required for rigorous inference.",
    "Unequal sample sizes across groups (n ranges from 3323 to 48846) could impact the power and robustness of the F-test, although ANOVA is generally robust to unequal n if variances are equal."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a linear mixed-effects model (LME) for each response variable (with appropriate transformations for non-normal data) including 'Stim Paradigm' as a fixed effect and 'Mouse' as a random intercept to properly account for the hierarchical data structure and repeated measures."
}
